tasks.verified: Verifies the panel's two rulings landed in artifacts: the week-end-field rule with part-of-day insulation on every preference_to carrier, the clock-time scenario asserting exactly n_offer_3 with its floor intact, delta confined to extraction descriptions versus v60, the gate still failing v56, and an eleventh red-proof mutation proving deletion of the new rule is caught.
tasks.spec:
You are implementing the unanimous rulings of a four-lane independent review panel on an SMS booking pathway. BOUNDARY: write only inside your task directory; never call an API, never mint, never git commit. You own exactly six output files: build_v61.py, v61_graph.json, scenarios.py, check_candidate_gate.py, redproof_run.py, report.md. Copy build_v60.py, scenarios.py, check_candidate_gate.py and redproof_run.py from ./source/ and edit the copies; run build_v61.py to produce v61_graph.json (adjust its output filename constant).

READ ./source/PANEL-RULINGS.txt COMPLETELY FIRST. Four independent reviewers ruled on two live diagnostic failures and agreed unanimously. Their prescriptions, not your own judgment, are what you implement.

RULING 1, a REAL patient-facing defect. Input 'next week in the morning please' offered 08/10 when the owner-binding meaning of next week was 08/03 through 08/07. Root cause, named identically by all four lanes: the extraction guidance specifies the START field for a week with no weekday but never specifies the matching END field, and a part-of-day mention leaks into the weekday default. FIX, in build_v61.py, in the preference_to extraction description on EVERY node that carries it: state that when the patient names a week qualifier but no weekday, preference_from is the week phrase alone and preference_to is friday followed by that same full week qualifier, giving the pair 'next week' through 'friday next week'; and state explicitly that a part of day such as morning or afternoon is NOT a weekday and does not change this week-only range. Keep the existing preference_from start rule byte-identical. The measured gateway receipt behind this: the pair from='next week' to='friday next week' returned 136 slots spanning exactly 08/03 through 08/07 on a verified Monday. The model must never compute a calendar date; it passes phrases through.

RULING 2, an INCORRECT test expectation. Input 'after 3pm works for me' correctly routed to the late band and offered 3:00 pm and 3:15 pm on the correct date, honoring the floor, but the scenario allowed only the first two offer bands. FIX, in scenarios.py, scenario 'clock time with no day at all': set expect_node to exactly the string 'n_offer_3'. All four lanes preferred this stricter single-node form over merely widening the list, because the routing contract deterministically classifies 'after 3pm' as late and a loose list would hide future routing regressions. Keep its expect_slot_floor and every other field unchanged. Change no other scenario. Count stays 30.

CHANGE 3, check_candidate_gate.py: extend the temporal invariant so the gate FAILS any graph whose preference_to guidance lacks the week-end rule ('friday next week' as the week-with-no-weekday end) — the blind spot that let this defect through was a gate that checked the start field and never the end field. Keep every other invariant untouched; the gate must still FAIL source/v56_graph.json.

CHANGE 4, redproof_run.py: add an ELEVENTH mutation that deletes the week-end-field rule from a preference_to description and prove the extended gate catches it. The printed line becomes mutations_caught=11 and the registered mutation name must mention preference_to, week_end, friday_next or end_field.

Scope discipline: compared to source/v60_graph.json your graph may differ ONLY in extraction descriptions. Same nodes, same routing, same prompts, same bodies, same variable names. The grading check enforces this mechanically.

OUTPUT CONTRACT for report.md: '# v61 Panel Rulings Implemented' then '## Summary' (max 3 bullets), '## Ruling 1' quoting your final preference_to description once in full, '## Ruling 2' showing the scenario diff, '## Gate And Redproof Extensions', '## Assumptions'. Under 600 words.
